tier_reason: Independent third-party run (Vello CPU author, unaffiliated with AGG, Skia or Cairo) of the public Blend2D bl_bench harness (LaurenzV/blend2d-apps bl_bench/backend_agg.cpp, backend_skia.cpp, backend_cairo.cpp; CMakeLists.txt) with the CPU model in the result file; compiler, compiler version and flags are not recorded and Skia/Cairo were prebuilt packages, so not A. I recomputed every ratio from the rcpms values and they match the record.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 367 stars, 92 forks (GitHub copy of the SourceForge AGG SVN); AGG 2.4 itself is widely vendored, e.g. by matplotlib's Agg backend
corrections.claimed_speedup: Apple M1 Pro, 2026-06-08 run, single-threaded, geometric mean of per-cell rcpms ratios over the 522 cells AGG shares with each baseline (29 tests x Solid/Linear/Radial x 6 sizes; derived from page data): 1.21x Skia (faster in 66% of cells; strokes 1.39x, fills 1.08x; 1.03x at 8x8, 1.02x at 16x16, 1.22x at 32x32, 1.39x at 64x64, 1.34x at 128x128, 1.28x at 256x256) and 2.29x Cairo 1.18.4 (faster in 94% of cells). The three earlier M1 runs (2025-09-24, 2026-01-22, 2026-05-17) give 1.20-1.21x Skia and 2.27-2.30x Cairo. Intel Core i9-14900K Windows run of 2026-01-22 (no Skia in that dataset): 1.87x Cairo 1.18.2 (1.89x on 2025-09-14). Slower than Blend2D 0.12.0 single-threaded (0.30x). All ratios derived from page data.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated in the result files. Harness: Blend2D bl_bench from LaurenzV/blend2d-apps built with CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (C++17); AGG compiled from source as the copy bundled in blend2d-apps/3rdparty/agg plus the Agg2D wrapper in 3rdparty/agg2d; Skia linked from the vcpkg unofficial-skia package and Cairo from pkg-config, both prebuilt with unrecorded build flags; compiler and version unstated. The exact harness commit used for the 2026 runs is not recorded.
corrections.workload: Blend2D bl_bench suite as run by LaurenzV (vello_chart): 29 tests (FillRectA/U/Rot, FillRoundU/Rot, FillTriangle, FillPoly NZ/EO with 10/20/40 vertices, Fill/Stroke Butterfly, Fish, Dragon, World, and the matching stroke tests) x paint styles x 6 sizes 8x8 to 256x256, SrcOver, 512x600 PRGB32 target, single thread, best of repeated runs reported as render calls per ms. The AGG backend supports only Solid, Linear and Radial styles (87 of 174 test/style rows). It fills integer-aligned solid rectangles through Agg2D::fillRectangleI (a direct span blend with no rasterizer) and draws radial gradients as centred radials, while Skia and Cairo draw a two-point conical gradient with a focal point.
corrections.caveats: Measured code is not this repository but the AGG 2.4-line copy bundled in blend2d-apps/3rdparty/agg, driven through the Agg2D wrapper; its hot-path headers (agg_basics.h, agg_rasterizer_scanline_aa.h, agg_rasterizer_cells_aa.h, agg_pixfmt_rgba.h) match ghaerr/agg-2.6 except for std:: qualifiers and a configurable cell_block_limit, so the result transfers. Against Skia (rows = test x style, geomean over sizes) AGG wins 67 of 87 rows: the polygon and path fills (FillPoly 1.06-1.35x by test, only FillPolyNZi10/Radial slightly behind at 0.98x; FillFish 1.54x, FillDragon 1.30x, FillWorld 1.27x, FillButterfly 1.21x) and every stroke except StrokeRectA (StrokeWorld 1.92x, StrokeFish 1.82x, StrokeButterfly 1.67x, StrokeRectU 1.60x); it loses the simple-shape fills FillRectA (0.84x, except solid), FillRectU (0.90x), FillRectRot (0.85x), FillRoundU (0.80x), FillRoundRot (0.94x), FillTriangle (0.94x) and StrokeRectA (0.52x). At 8x8 and 16x16 it is only at parity overall. Against Cairo it wins 84 of 87 rows, losing StrokeRectA/Solid (0.33x), FillRectU/Solid (0.46x) and FillRectA/Linear (0.91x). Both libraries run single-threaded and anti-aliased; AGG's radial gradient is the simpler centred form (radial rows 1.13x vs linear 1.25x against Skia), and output equivalence is not checked in the published data. This GitHub copy was cloned from the SourceForge SVN at r132 (2019-05-06) and last changed on 2023-08-21; the SourceForge SVN continued to r145 (2024-09-28: C++20/23 warning fixes, and r144 moved the bundled General Polygon Clipper to MIT). In this copy GPC is still under its non-commercial licence, so do not copy agg-src/gpc (the core is BSD-3-Clause or the AGG Public License). Skia's version is not recorded in the data.

notes: Ratios reproduce exactly and are stable across all four M1 runs. Do not treat ghaerr/agg-2.6 as the canonical AGG: it is a 2019 clone of the official SourceForge SVN with a few merged PRs and a 2023-08-21 last commit, while SourceForge (https://sourceforge.net/projects/agg/, svn r145, 2024-09-28) is upstream and ahead (and has GPC under MIT); keep ghaerr as the convenient GitHub link with is_fork_of pointing to SourceForge. Usability is mixed only because of the non-commercial GPC files in this copy.

tier_reason: Independent third-party run (Vello CPU author, unaffiliated with JUCE, Skia or Cairo) of the public Blend2D bl_bench harness (LaurenzV/blend2d-apps bl_bench/backend_juce.cpp, backend_skia.cpp, backend_cairo.cpp; JUCE 8.0.8 recorded in the result file) on a named CPU; compiler, version and flags are not recorded, so not A. My recomputation of the ratios matches the record.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Apple M1 Pro, 2026-06-08 run, JUCE 8.0.8 software renderer, single-threaded, geometric mean of per-cell rcpms ratios over 870 cells (29 tests x Solid/Linear/Radial/Pattern_NN/Pattern_BI x 6 sizes; derived from page data): 1.68x Skia (faster in 84% of cells; strokes 2.10x, fills 1.40x; 1.26x at 8x8, 1.32x at 16x16, 1.69x at 32x32, 2.02x at 64x64 and 128x128, 1.97x at 256x256) and 2.93x Cairo 1.18.4 (faster in 95% of cells). Excluding the three StrokeRect tests, which JUCE draws as four filled rectangles instead of a stroked path: 1.64x Skia and 2.90x Cairo. Earlier M1 runs give 1.61-1.70x Skia and 2.79-2.94x Cairo. Slower than Blend2D 0.12.0 single-threaded (0.41x). No JUCE run in the x86 data. All ratios derived from page data.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated in the result files. Harness: Blend2D bl_bench from LaurenzV/blend2d-apps, CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (C++17); JUCE 8.0.8 compiled from source via JUCE_DIR/add_subdirectory with -DJUCE_USE_CURL=0 -DUSE_COREGRAPHICS_RENDERING=0 and a juce::SoftwareImageType surface; Skia from the vcpkg unofficial-skia package and Cairo from pkg-config, both prebuilt with unrecorded flags; compiler and version unstated.
corrections.caveats: Some tests do different work from the baselines. JUCE's Graphics::drawRect fills four rectangles inside the shape bounds (LowLevelGraphicsContext::drawRect) instead of stroking a centred mitred path, so StrokeRectA/U/Rot are not like-for-like (StrokeRectU 3.44x Skia). JUCE's radial paint is a centred radial with no focal point, while Skia and Cairo draw a two-point conical gradient. JUCE's EdgeTable rasterizer is anti-aliased but uses its own approximate coverage (8-bit fixed-point x with adaptive vertical sub-steps), and output equivalence is not checked in the published data. All renderers here run single-threaded. Against Skia (rows = test x style, geomean over sizes) JUCE wins 134 of 145 rows, with the largest gains on strokes (StrokeWorld 3.08x, StrokeFish 2.47x, StrokeDragon 2.33x) and complex polygon fills (FillPolyEOi40 2.03x). It loses large solid and pattern rectangle fills (FillRectA/Solid 0.56x, down to 0.31x at 128x128 and 256x256), rotated nearest-neighbour pattern fills (FillRectRot 0.61x, FillRoundRot 0.72x) and FillRoundU/FillRectRot/FillTriangle solid (0.74-0.81x). Against Cairo it wins 138 of 145 rows, losing FillRectA (0.43-0.45x), FillRectU (0.59-0.68x) and StrokeRectA/Solid (0.71x). Only one machine (M1 Pro). JUCE 8.0.8 was measured; the repository is now at 9.0.3 (2026-09-28). The harness's AGG/Cairo/Skia/JUCE backends come from the Blend2D author and the runs from the Vello CPU author, both competitors but independent of JUCE; the Skia version is not recorded. Licence: the JUCE modules, juce_graphics included, are dual-licensed AGPLv3 / commercial JUCE licence, so closed-source or non-AGPL use needs the commercial licence (the README asks tools to tell users this).

notes: Ratios reproduce exactly and hold across all four M1 runs. The claim stands at 1.64x Skia even after dropping the StrokeRect tests JUCE does differently. The record's caveat that JUCE trails Skia on small fills was wrong: its losses are on large solid and pattern rectangle fills, so I rewrote the caveat. Metadata (AGPL-3.0, 8.9k stars, last commit 2026-09-28) is correct.

tier_reason: Independent third-party run of the public bl_bench harness (LaurenzV/blend2d-apps benching branch bl_bench/backend_raqote.cpp via LaurenzV/raqote_c, raqote 0.8.5 per Cargo.lock) on named CPUs, with compiler and C++ flags unrecorded, so B at most. The claim is overstated: the raqote backend's rotated tests are broken (see caveats), and with them removed raqote is slower than Skia and wins against Cairo only on the M1.

corrections.baseline: Cairo (image surface; 1.18.4 on the M1 Pro run, 1.18.2 on the Windows x86 run); not faster than Skia once the broken rotated tests are excluded
corrections.claimed_speedup: Apple M1 Pro, 2026-06-08 run, single-threaded. As published, geometric means of per-cell rcpms ratios are 1.08x Skia (1044 cells, faster in 57%) and 1.84x Cairo 1.18.4 (870 cells), but the four rotated tests are inflated by a harness bug. Excluding FillRectRot, FillRoundRot, StrokeRectRot and StrokeRoundRot: 0.93x Skia (900 cells, faster in 51%; fills 1.08x, strokes 0.77x), i.e. not faster than Skia, and 1.48x Cairo (750 cells, faster in 76%; fills 1.86x, strokes 1.11x). The earlier M1 runs give the same picture (0.92-0.93x Skia, 1.46-1.49x Cairo). Intel Core i9-14900K Windows run of 2026-01-22 (no Skia): 1.09x Cairo 1.18.2 as published, 0.89x with the rotated tests excluded (fills 1.19x, strokes 0.61x). Slower than Blend2D 0.12.0 single-threaded (0.26x as published). All ratios derived from page data.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust crates (raqote 0.8.5 through the raqote_c staticlib, cargo build --release) built with target-feature=+avx2 on x86 and default NEON on ARM (LaurenzV master thesis Section 5.2); C++ harness CMake Release; Skia from the vcpkg unofficial-skia package and Cairo from pkg-config, both prebuilt with unrecorded flags; rustc and C++ compiler versions are not stated.
corrections.workload: Blend2D bl_bench suite with the raqote backend from LaurenzV/blend2d-apps (benching branch, bl_bench/backend_raqote.cpp) calling raqote 0.8.5 through the LaurenzV/raqote_c C bindings: 29 fill/stroke tests x six paint styles (Solid, Linear, Radial, Conic, Pattern_NN, Pattern_BI) x six sizes 8x8 to 256x256, SrcOver, 512x600 target, single thread, render calls per ms. In the rotated tests the raqote backend uses a random angle about each shape's own centre (as intended), unlike the incrementing angle about the screen centre used by the other backends, and its transform composition is wrong (see caveats).
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1.2k stars, 65 forks; README lists resvg, Servo and orbtk as users (the list may be dated)
corrections.caveats: Harness bug: backend_raqote.cpp builds the rotation as rq_transform_multiply(rq_transform_multiply(translate_to_centre, rotate), translate_back), and raqote_c implements rq_transform_multiply(a, b) as euclid a.then(b). Each shape is therefore rotated about the canvas origin by a random angle in [0, 6.28), so most rotated shapes land off the 512x600 canvas and are clipped. The data shows it: raqote's FillRectRot at 256x256 (29.4 calls/ms) is 4.3x faster than its own FillRectU (6.82), and FillRoundRot (32.2) is 4.8x faster than FillRoundU (6.76), while every other single-threaded renderer is slower on the rotated variants at 64x64 and 256x256. That is where the published 3.16x/3.09x/2.59x/2.12x wins over Skia on FillRectRot/FillRoundRot/StrokeRectRot/StrokeRoundRot (and 9.49x on FillRectRot over Cairo) come from. With those tests excluded raqote wins only 75 of 150 test x style rows against Skia (99 of 125 against Cairo): path and complex-polygon fills (FillWorld 1.77x, FillPolyEOi40 1.44x, FillFish 1.43x, FillButterfly and FillDragon 1.35x). It loses StrokeRectA (0.28x), FillRectA (0.68x), StrokeWorld (0.55x), StrokeRoundU (0.65x), StrokeRectU (0.69x), StrokeTriangle (0.71x), FillRoundU (0.79x) and FillRectU (0.86x), and is 0.90x at 256x256. Against Cairo the wins are fills; it loses rectangle fills (FillRectA 0.57x, FillRectU 0.61x), StrokeRectA (0.37x), StrokeRectU (0.71x) and StrokeWorld (0.64x), and on the x86 run it is slower overall. raqote anti-aliases with 4x4 multisampling (thesis Section 4.1, coarser coverage than analytic rasterizers) and has no SIMD code or threading; output equivalence is not checked in the data. Language is Rust: it falls outside the C++ filter, and from C++ it is reachable only through the unofficial raqote_c shim ('not meant for production'). raqote 0.8.5 (2024-07-24) was measured; the last commit was 2025-02-11. The runner (Vello CPU author) wrote both the raqote backend and the bindings; the Skia version is not recorded.

notes: Downgraded because the claim is overstated. A transform-order bug in the runner's raqote backend inflates the four rotated tests, and with them removed raqote is 0.93x Skia (slower), 1.48x Cairo on M1 and 0.89x Cairo on x86 (all derived). The record already has language Rust; the orchestrator should keep that as an override and flag the C++ filter mismatch. Consider a retier to C or reference status if the catalog wants only clean C++-callable entries; license BSD-3-Clause, stale status and 2025-02-11 last commit are correct.
